blocks.text: In 1987, agnès b. travelled to Moscow, then the capital of the Soviet Union, for five days, accompanied by Philippe Trétiack, journalist and writer for ELLE magazine. Her mission: to discover new fashions, new styles and new tastes, in a country and among a population about which she then knew almost nothing.

On arrival, she found herself plunged into a world far removed from her Western points of reference: silent crowds, immense spaces, a difficult daily life, and clothes that were often dark and plain. But over the course of those five days, her gaze shifted. Armed with her film Nikon, agnès b. began to photograph, for herself, what she discovered as she moved around Moscow. Children huddled against their parents, shopkeepers in astonishing outfits, passers-by, faces, attitudes, clothes: so many details that caught her attention and fed her pleasure in discovery.

In black and white as well as in colour, these photographs were thus born almost spontaneously, alongside the report she was producing for ELLE. They testify less to a desire to document the Soviet Union than to the curious, attentive eye that agnès b. turns on people and on everything around her.

Through these candid images emerges the Moscow of 1987, only a few years before the disappearance of the Soviet Union: a city and an era captured through a multitude of ordinary scenes, encounters and details that surprised, amused or moved agnès b. during those five days.
